# Jubilees Chapter 50 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Sabbath legislation; the book's eschatological close

---

**50:1** After this law I made known to you the Sabbaths of the land, the Sabbath years, and the jubilees, from the days of Adam. And the LORD commanded you to observe the Sabbath on the day of rest.

**50:2** Every man who does any work on it, or who goes on a journey, or who conducts business, or who draws water that had not been prepared the day before, or who lifts any burden to carry it out of his tent or out of his house — that man shall die.

**50:3** You shall do no work whatever on the Sabbath day, except what you have prepared on the sixth day to eat and drink — resting and keeping Sabbath from all work on that day, and blessing the LORD your God, who has given you this day of festival and holy day and a day of the holy kingdom for all Israel.

**50:4** This day is greater than all days. On this day you shall be holy; you shall rest from all work.

**50:5** Whoever profanes this day, whoever does any work on it, shall die. Whoever profanes it shall die.

**50:6** You shall not light a fire in any of your dwellings on the Sabbath day. You shall not prepare food on the Sabbath. Prepare all your food on the sixth day before the Sabbath.

**50:7** You shall not carry anything out or into the house on the Sabbath.

**50:8** You shall not move anything from house to house on the Sabbath.

**50:9** You shall do nothing on the Sabbath day except bless the LORD your God.

**50:10** Whoever carries a burden out of his dwelling on the Sabbath shall die.

**50:11** Whoever goes on a journey on the Sabbath day — for the purpose of business or travel away from home — that person shall die.

**50:12** Whoever draws a sword or bow on the Sabbath, or takes up any implement of war, shall die.

**50:13** Whoever catches an animal, bird, or fish on the Sabbath shall die.

**50:14** Whoever does any of the following on the Sabbath shall die: any work; any journey; tilling a field; plowing; cutting anything; lighting a fire; loading a beast; sailing a ship; striking or killing anything; slaughtering a beast or bird; catching fish; fasting; or waging war.

**50:15** The person who does any of these things on the Sabbath shall die, so that the children of Israel may observe the Sabbath according to the Sabbath commandments, as written in the tablets which he gave me to write down for you — the law of every appointed time.

**50:16** Here is the completion of the account of the divisions of the days. From the day of creation until the day when the new creation is made — when the heavens and the earth and all their creatures shall be renewed, like the powers of the sky and all the creatures of the earth — until the day when the sanctuary of the LORD shall be made in Jerusalem on Mount Zion: all the years and all the days shall be hallowed and consecrated from that time until this.

**50:17** The whole account of the divisions of the days of the law and of the testimony has now been completed. You gave it to Moses on Mount Sinai, until the new creation is made, when the sanctuary of the LORD shall be built in Jerusalem for all eternity.

---

*LOGOS notes: Chapter 50 is the culminating chapter of Jubilees and contains the most comprehensive Sabbath legislation in any Second Temple text. The death penalty is prescribed for an extraordinarily wide range of activities including — most strikingly — fasting on the Sabbath (v.14), which reflects Jubilees' anti-ascetic Sabbath theology: the Sabbath is a day of joy, not deprivation. The eschatological conclusion (vv.16-17) frames the entire book as a disclosure that runs from creation to new creation, with the Jerusalem sanctuary as the ultimate telos.*
